chunks: Al-Faqih: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn via his reliable chain from Abdallah ibn al-Mughira from more than one of our companions from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him)

In regards to two men who had two Dirhams between them, one of them said: 'The two Dirhams are mine,' and the other said: 'They are between me and you,' he said: 'As for the one who said: 'They are between me and you,' then he has acknowledged that one of the two Dirhams is not his and that it belongs to his companion, and the remaining one is divided between them.'
ai.seo_question: How is property divided between two claimants when one asserts full ownership and the other asserts shared ownership?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Faqih illustrates the principle of *al-istishab* (presumption of continuity) and evidentiary weight in Shia jurisprudence, where the claimant of partial ownership effectively concedes the other's share. It highlights the scholarly emphasis on logical consistency in testimony, where admitting a portion for the opponent validates the division of the remainder. This case serves as a foundational example for resolving disputes over movable property when clear documentation is absent.

en.ammaar-muslim: 1. [1/113] al-Faqih: Muhammad b. Ali b. al-Husayn via his reliable chain to Abdallah b. al-Mughira from more than one of our companions from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام

in regards two men who have two Dirhams between them, one of them says: they are both mine, while the other says: they are between me and you (one is mine and the other is yours), he said: as for the one who says: ‘they are between me and you’ then he has acknowledged that one of the Dirhams is not his and that it belongs to his fellow (he has already abandoned his claim over one of the Dirhams), and the remaining one is divided between them (i.e. each one gets a half).
